svg.title: What `hpr mc validation/fixtures/ork/guides/level-1.ork --runs 200 --seed 2026 --mass-sd 0.02 --drag-sd 0.05 --impulse-sd 0.03` prints, as a terminal shows it
svg.desc: The command line, then each line it printed, long lines wrapped; balloons A, B, C mark the lines the page explains. Drawn by cargo xtask cli from the same run as the page's text.
svg.text: $ hpr mc validation/fixtures/ork/guides/level-1.ork --runs 200 --seed 2026 --mass-sd 0.02
--drag-sd 0.05 --impulse-sd 0.03
Level 1 guide rocket (level-1.ork)
configuration 1 of 2: [H170M-10]
help: --config flies the others, by number or name: 2 [I175WS-9]
200 simulated flights, seed 2026: 0 failed
nominal mean std dev 5% median 95%
landing distance (m) 0.7 0.7 0.0 0.7 0.7 0.8
landing distance (ft) 2 2 0 2 2 3
200 of 200 flights landed, centered 0.7 m (2 ft) west and 0.0 m (0 ft) north of the pad
landing ellipse semi-major semi-minor heading flights inside
95%, the next flight 0.1 m (0 ft) 0.0 m (0 ft) 090° T 98.5%
motor: 1 × H170M (from the bundled catalog, as of 2026-09-17) in `Motor mount tube`, lit at launch
launched at 0.00000° N, 0.00000° E, 0 m (0 ft) above sea level, from a 1.5 m (4.9 ft) vertical
rail, in calm air
scattered, one standard deviation each: --mass-sd 0.02, --drag-sd 0.05, --impulse-sd 0.03
note: the file's 1 recovery device flies as OpenRocket flies it. Each opens fully at its event,
with the file's drag coefficient or OpenRocket's own. Once one opens, the rocket descends as a
point under the open devices' drag alone
warning: drag, the nominal flight: issue #67: a cone-like nose's or shoulder's pressure drag reads
high from Mach 0.8 (about twice a measured cone's at Mach 0.85, still +15% at 1.5). So the
apogee, the top speed and the drift read low. The flutter margin and the largest dynamic
pressure look better than they are. This flight reaches Mach 0.84 at 1.7 s
(https://github.com/nrdptel/fusionspace-eridanus/issues/67)
warning: drag, the nominal flight: issue #68: base drag reads high from Mach 0.8 to 1.2 (0.225
against a measured 0.156 at Mach 0.9). So the apogee, the top speed and the drift read low. The
flutter margin and the largest dynamic pressure look better than they are. This flight reaches
Mach 0.84 at 1.7 s (https://github.com/nrdptel/fusionspace-eridanus/issues/68)
warning: drag, the nominal flight: issue #18: skin friction is taken as fully turbulent, but on a
smooth surface the flow stays laminar near the nose, where friction is lower. HPR Sim's drag
reads high by 3.6% on RocketPy's Calisto at Mach 0.3. If this surface is that smooth, the drag
reads high. So the apogee, the top speed and the drift read low. The flutter margin and the
largest dynamic pressure look better than they are
(https://github.com/nrdptel/fusionspace-eridanus/issues/18)
warning: stability, the nominal flight: issue #172: the static margin read up to 0.1108 calibers
higher than OpenRocket's on four private designs, for a reason not yet found. This flight's
margin may read high by as much (https://github.com/nrdptel/fusionspace-eridanus/issues/172)
How far to trust it. Simulated from the design file, not measured; the spread above comes from the
inputs' scatter alone, not from the model's error. Against 53 logged flights of fliers' own designs,
the simulated apogee averaged 8.7% above the logged one. Each logged apogee is the height climbed in
the day's air. The simulated apogee was within 10% on 26 and read low on 13, by at most 20%. Plan a
waiver or a field's ceiling with room above this apogee; the altimeter's reading is the one to log,
and the RSO decides.
More: https://hpr.fusionspace.co/accuracy.html
